title: Biomedical AI Quality and Safety Simulator
audience: Basic science learners exploring AI quality, safety, drift, calibration, and transparency
objectives: Recognize covariate shift in a simulated sepsis prediction model.
Compare doing nothing versus retraining under distribution shift.
Evaluate vendor model discrimination and calibration on a mismatched local population.
Build a model card documenting intended use, limitations, metrics, and ethical considerations.

sections.name: Sepsis Drift
sections.purpose: Show how input distribution changes can degrade model behavior.
sections.how_to_use: Move the months slider, compare original and current lactate distributions, and test whether retraining changes false positive rate.

sections.name: Vendor Calibration
sections.purpose: Compare ranking performance with probability reliability.
sections.how_to_use: Adjust population mismatch, review AUC, and inspect whether the calibration curve follows the diagonal.

sections.name: Model Card Builder
sections.how_to_use: Fill in model name, developer, intended users, caveats, and ethical considerations, then review the generated model card.

chatbot_guidance: When asked how to use this notebook, guide the learner through the three tabs: drift, calibration, and model card.
For basic science users, emphasize distribution shift, evaluation limits, calibration, and transparent documentation.
Explain that high AUC does not guarantee well-calibrated probabilities.
